gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a dated maker-store price for the screens ChatGPT picked, so none shows that two of its price cards are above the maker's own price today (Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro: $365.99 on ChatGPT's card, $207.99 on mobilepixels.us; Kwumsy S7 16": $339.99 on the card, $269.99 on kwumsy.com). None states that INVZI says its $399 MagHub Dual Lite 16", ChatGPT's top pick, cannot run two independent extended displays on standard M1/M2/M3 MacBooks.
standout_why: I compared against the two itechguides pages ChatGPT cited and the two top results, The Office Journal and WorkCocoon '16-inch'. Neither itechguides page prices the Duex Float 2 Pro, the MagHub, the Kwumsy models or the Flexpire. The only Mobile Pixels prices on the 2026 itechguides page are Lenovo 'when crawled' figures with no date: Trio 3.0 Pro at $441.99 promo / $519.99, and Glance 16 at $152.99 / $179.99. The Office Journal and WorkCocoon list only no-name Amazon 16" monitors (Redalf, Orfibz, Ozirex, Blackview). They give no dollar prices, no video path and no fit range. No rival page states how many external displays a MacBook drives. None mentions the MagHub base-M-chip limit.
decides: This confirms the stacked single 16-inch screen that ChatGPT itself said it preferred. The Duex Float 2 Pro (ours) is 16" 2560×1600 at 120 Hz, and Mobile Pixels says it fits 15–16" laptops. Today it costs {price:mobile-pixels-duex-float-2-pro} on the maker store. ChatGPT's card for it showed $365.99. It also undercuts the ViewSonic VG1656-2K ($329.99, 60 Hz), which is ChatGPT's 'best standalone' pick. For two added screens, the MagHub Dual Lite's $399 is today's real price. INVZI's own page rules it out for base M1–M3 MacBooks, so on those laptops it loses to a one-screen stacked setup. Kwumsy's N3 at $149.99 is the cheapest two-screen 16" model I priced. I could not open its fit range or video path, so it cannot win on a sourced compatibility claim.
